content.thinking:
Still all peaks equal — because with 8192 anchors over 512 nodes × 512 phases, nearly every cell is anchored (bound 0), so the peak = max local drift over one interval, independent of g. The message edges don't matter.

To get a realistic worst case where all 8 Dijkstras run and matter, let me reduce the anchors. Let me make a variant with sparse anchors: anchors = [[i, 0, 1] for i in range(0, N, 64)] (a few nodes anchored at one phase).

Let me create big3.py with sparse anchors and re-time the full plan + audit.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/tmp && python3 - << 'PYEOF'
p='big2.py'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("""anchors = []
while len(anchors) < 8192:
    a,b = rr(0,P); anchors.append([rng.randrange(N), a, b])""",
"""anchors = [[i, p, p+1] for i in range(0, N, 64) for p in range(0, P, 64)]""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
PYEOF
python3 big2.py 1 plan > big_plan4.jsonl 2>big_plan4.err; cat big_plan4.err
cd /workspace && time (python3 -B submission/main.py < tmp/big_plan4.jsonl > tmp/big_plan4.out); ls -la tmp/big_plan4.out; python3 -c "
import json; d=json.load(open('/workspace/tmp/big_plan4.out')); print('peaks',d['peaks_as'],'guard',d['guard_ns'],'warm',d['warmup_cycle'])"
